messages:
Anya (prod): ran a multi-tenant fairness sim comparing reserved pools vs shared lanes. attaching CSV + heatmaps. quick summary: when tenant T3 spikes (x10 for 60s) reserved tenants see ~8% higher p99 vs baseline, shared lanes absorb tails but cost goes up ~2.3x. curious about acceptable mitigations
capacity-sim-bot: sim-run-id=sim-2024-11-05-03 summary: baseline p50/p90/p99 reserved=12/45/180ms; under spike reserved p50/p90/p99=15/60/195ms; shared p50/p90/p99=14/55/340ms; cost-multiplier(shared)=2.3x; logs + heatmaps: https://s3.redwood/sim/sim-2024-11-05-03.zip
Matt (infra): thanks, can you paste the sim config (seq lengths, queueing policy, preemptable=true/false)?
Anya (prod): sure — config snippet: ```
workload: mix
tenants: 20
seq_len_dist: {short:0.6, medium:0.3, long:0.1}
spike: {tenant:T3, factor:10, duration_s:60}
admission: FIFO
preempt: enabled, preempt_delay_s=5
quant: int8
```
Priya (sre): ops concern: preempt=enabled w/ 5s delay creates cascading retries for short requests. if reserved tenants are preempted they retry -> queue pressure -> higher p99. we should test a soft-preempt mode (delay + backoff)
Eva (eng): +1 on soft-preempt. alternative: soft-quotas with spillover cap so reserved tenants keep a baseline GPU share and unused reserve can be borrowed but capped per-window. that reduces tail impact on reserved customers while allowing burst absorb.
Caroline (pm): from a product POV customers buying reserved capacity want predictability. we should define launch criteria: 1) p99 for reserved tenants under simulated spikes must be <= 1.2x baseline for 95% of runs, 2) cost delta vs current reserved mode <= 25% for typical workloads.
Matt (infra): implementation notes: soft-quotas require admission-layer change + bookkeeping per-tenant window. spillover cap implies periodic reconciliation job. also billing change if we meter borrowed capacity.
Anya (prod): proposal: prototype soft-quota with parameters: baseline_share=1.0 (configured), spillover_pct=12%, spillover_window_s=300, preempt_delay_s=15. run 100 sims sweep over spike intensity [2x,5x,10x].
Priya (sre): i'll run sensitivity sweep. will include preempt_delay values [5,15,30] and retry/backoff behavior. target finish by next Wed.
Eva (eng): i'll carve a staging branch to implement admission + soft quota logic, name: feat/soft-quota-spillover. ETA: 2w for spike prototype. I'll add a simple metrics dashboard: per-tenant borrowed_tokens, spillover_events.
Matt (infra): note: we should also surface a per-tenant "spillover used" flag in the console for billing/alerts. ops will need alert thresholds.
Caroline (pm): action item: add launch gating criteria to roadmap doc (p99 SLA + cost delta + billing UX). i'll own the gating doc.
Anya (prod): action list:
- Priya: run sim sensitivity sweep (due: next Wed)
- Eva: prototype soft-quota admission in staging (due: 2w)
- Matt: spec reconciliation job + console flag (sync with Eva, due: 3w)
- Caroline: write launch gating doc and customer comm plan (due: 1w)
- Anya: collect sim artifacts and run customer-impact mapping (due: 10d)
Priya (sre): ack. I'll include a stresstest with client retry patterns to catch retry storms.
Eva (eng): will post branch PR when ready and include a small harness to replay sim traces.
Anya (prod): decision for now: greenlight Q2 spike for soft-quota + spillover prototype. not a GA commit yet; need to validate gating criteria. :thumbsup:
Matt (infra): one more ask — add a fallback policy: if spillover usage > 60% for 5m, throttle spillover and notify ops. otherwise risk sustained cost blowouts.
Caroline (pm): agreed. add to gating doc. also let's collect customer cases who requested both "predictable latency" and "burst absorb" so we can prioritize UI billing options.
Anya (prod): thanks all — I'll create a follow-up thread for spike results. closing this sync for now.
